name: Natural Dyed Easter Eggs using Red Beets, Blueberries & Yellow Turmeric

instructions.primary_message: This recipe contains steps that can be done by smaller hands! You know your child (and their cooking abilities) best, so get them involved where you feel comfortable. Have fun!

Wash, dry, peel, and trim beets; roughly chop. Place in a medium saucepan, along with water, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool completely.

Wash, dry, and place blueberries in another medium saucepan, then mash with a fork or potato masher. Add water and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool completely.

Finally, place water and turmeric in a third medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat; once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool completely.

Meanwhile, place water in a 6-quart multicooker, then add the metal trivet. Arrange eggs on the trivet in an even layer, then lock lid and set to pressure cook on HIGH for 7 minutes. Once done, manually release the pressure. (Alternatively, you can hard boil the eggs using the stovetop.)
While the eggs are cooking, fill a medium bowl halfway with cold water (from the tap) and add 12 ice cubes, creating an ice bath.
When the eggs are done, use a slotted spoon or tongs to add them to the ice bath. Set aside to cool completely, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, use a strainer to remove solids from the cooled dyes, then transfer each to a large jar or storage container. Add 1 tablespoon of vinegar to each jar and stir to combine.

Divide eggs between the jars. Allow eggs to sit for 1 hour, then remove to a paper towel-lined plate and allow to dry. Resubmerge eggs in the dye for 1-hour periods, allowing eggs to dry after each, until desired color is reached. Refrigerate dyed eggs.
Display your naturally dyed eggs and enjoy!
